TransportPipes · design document · October 21, 2026

Version 1.1: a clear path, a fair map, faster hands

Four players and a district full of tenants played v1.0 for a day. This document turns what they ran into into the next version: what they got stuck on, why, and how v1.1 changes it. Everything here works on the running world: no server wipe.

A · What do I do next?An advisor with the three best next steps, a level roadmap, and Loady's second chapter.
B · Every estate can playA guaranteed starter kit: copper, coal, stone and a pond in reach. Surveyors bring it to existing estates.
C · Trade with who you choseDirect partners only: no trading through other estates, no district-sized networks.
D · ControlsLeft-drag selects, right-drag pans. Select many buildings and upgrade them together, paint rows of panels.
E · A calm screenFixed zones: guidance left, one inspector right, big windows in the middle, nothing on top of each other.
F · Shipped alreadyEighteen fixes from the play day, from storage clarity to cheaper pipes: listed at the end.

How to read this

Each theme starts with what we saw, explains why it happens (with numbers from the game where we have them), then shows the design: rules, mockups and the decisions, with the reasons. The last pages are the plan to build it, in order, with how each part is checked. Mockups are drawn in the game's own style; screenshots are from the play day and from the automated play scripts.

The design pillars (unchanged)

PillarWhat it means for v1.1
Pipes are the gameTrade is a pipe you lay to a neighbour, not a menu. Controls make laying and managing pipes and buildings fast.
An idle game that respects your timeWhen you come back, the game tells you the three things worth doing, in a click each.
Expansion, not resetsNothing is wiped. New rules apply to the running world through migrations and surveys.
Multiplayer that feels localYour neighbours are the companies you pipe to. Far away companies are someone else's neighbours.

Four players and the tenants of one district (Capital) played for a day. One tester reported as they played; the screenshots on these pages are theirs.

2 · How a player plays the first days

A player opens the game a few times a day. Each visit has the same shape: see what changed → collect → invest → set something running → leave. The game is fun when every visit has an obvious good investment and a reason to come back.

The first three days, as the simulation plays them

The balance simulation (TheFirstSession, TheFirstDay, TheFirstTwoWeeks) plays like a player: one action at a time, sessions with breaks. After today's changes a typical player reaches:

Company LevelWhen (typical player)What it brings
2–4first session (Loady's steps)Iron Mine, Small Factory, Flower Bed, Lab
5after ~4½ hoursCopper Mine, Coal Pit, Sand Dredger, Lumber Camp, Water Pump, Sawmill, the first parcel (5,000 g)
6–7evening of day 1Smelter, Brickworks, Glassworks, parcel 2 at 7
10day 2Quarry, Warehouse, Engineer Workshop
15 · 20 · 25day 4 · 5½ · 8½Recycler · Expeditions, Showroom · the long middle game

What the tester did

They followed Loady through the tutorial, built a mine and factory chain, connected to neighbours, upgraded the moilies and the storage, and reached Level 5 in the first hours. Then the tutorial was over, and the goal tracker said only "Next: Company Level 6" and "This week: a new parcel at Level 7". Level 5 had unlocked six new buildings, and the estate could place almost none of them.

3 · Where the loop stalls: Company Level 5

The problemLevel 5 unlocks six buildings at once. Four need something most estates don't have in reach, so the reward for the level is a menu of things you can't use, and nothing says what to do instead.
Unlocked at Level 5NeedsTypical estate (start parcels + parcel 1)
Copper Minea copper depositnone copper exists only on Copper Gulch estates
Coal Pita coal deposit40% a 2×2 patch, often in a parcel for Level 12+
Sand Dredgera shore50% a pond, often in a later parcel
Water Pumpa shore50% same pond
Lumber Campforestyes every estate has a patch
Sawmillwood (from a Lumber Camp)yes

Counted on the play district (deposit tiles per estate):

EstateIronCopperCoalStoneWaterForest
A player (Sunny Flats)92244535
Ironvale Stone (tenant)9016290144
Ironvale Solar (tenant)9044046
A free estate9004061

And the parcels: deposits other than the starting iron are placed in random parcels, and the parcels unlock at Company Level 5, 7, 12, 14, 18, 25, 30… A coal patch in parcel 13 is out of reach until Level 30.

Three more things that make the middle feel aimless

  • Upgrades have no target. "Upgrade" is always possible and always a little useful; nothing says which one pays back best.
  • Research is a list. The tester had 438 research points and "pick one!" in the top bar, but no hint which tech helps their estate.
  • Daily orders and the week's goal are small. They don't point at the next chain to build.
Decisionv1.1 fixes the cause (B: every estate gets the basics within reach) and the symptom (A: the game always says what the best next steps are, and what the next levels bring).

4 · A · What do I do next? The advisor

The goal tracker on the left becomes "Next steps": the three best things to do right now, ranked, each with the reason in numbers and a Show me button that points at it (the same way Loady's steps do). It refreshes as the company changes, and when the player comes back after a break it is the first thing they see.

Next steps
1
Your factories are 29 energy short
2 Small Factories run at 52%: a Wind Moily (1,200 g) fixes it, +38 g/min
Show me
2
Upgrade Wind Moily #3 to level 10
Level 10 doubles it: 8,900 g, pays back in 41 min
Upgrade
3
Pick a research: Ore Washing
+25% iron ore for your 7 mines · you have 438 points
Open
Today: 230 energy for the hub · This week: parcel at Level 7

How the steps are chosen

Candidates are scored by gold per minute gained ÷ gold spent (payback), with a few rules on top:

KindWhen it shows
Shortagea network's buildings get less than they need (from the network view): the cheapest producer that fills it
Fulla full trading post or storage: upgrade it, or build another
Best upgradethe upgrade with the quickest payback; milestones (10, 25…) count their doubling
Next chaina new building that turns what you make into something worth more (ore → ingots → …)
Researchenough points and nothing researching: the tech that helps your buildings most
Parcela parcel you can afford, with what's in it ("copper and a pond")
Partnera neighbour who needs what you have spare, close enough to pay
Pumpa network short of pump stations (only once you can build them)

Rules

  • Always three, always doable. A step that needs more gold than the player has says when they'll have it ("in 12 min"), and never a locked building.
  • The numbers are the game's. The server computes the steps from the same flow solution the network view uses, so "29 short" here is the same 29 as there.
  • One click. Show me selects, moves the camera and opens the right tool; an upgrade step upgrades directly.
  • Quiet when it's good. When nothing is short or full, the steps are investments; the card can be collapsed.

5 · A · The level roadmap and Loady's second chapter

The level roadmap

The Company Level in the top bar already shows XP, XP per minute and the time to the next level; its breakdown says where the XP came from. v1.1 adds what the next levels bring, so a level is something to look forward to and to plan for.

Company Level 5 → 6 in 1 h 12 min
Level 6🏭 Smelter · 🧱 Brickworksyou have copper
Level 7🪟 Glassworks · parcel 210,000 g
Level 8🤝 Corporations · valves
Level 10⛏ Quarry · 📦 Warehouse · a manager
Open a level for its buildings and what they need.

Each row says what the level unlocks and, for buildings, whether the estate can use them ("you have copper", "needs a shore: parcel 6 has one"). It lives in the level breakdown and in the level-up celebration ("Level 6! Smelter and Brickworks: build a Smelter on your copper").

Why

Idle games keep players through anticipation: the next unlock should always be visible, close and concrete. Today the unlock is a surprise, and at Level 5 a disappointing one.

Loady's second chapter

The tutorial ends after eleven steps (around Level 5). Chapter 2 continues with goals that teach the middle game, one at a time, each with a reward. A returning player sees chapter 2 where they are; veterans skip it like chapter 1.

StepGoalTeaches
12Mine copper and smelt it (Copper Mine + Smelter)a second chain from the starter kit
13Upgrade a building to level 10milestones double output; the green badge
14Make bricks (Coal Pit + Brickworks, with stone)a three-input factory
15Finish three researchesresearch as a plan, not a list
16Deliver three daily ordersstorages and orders
17Earn 100 g/min from neighbourspartners close enough to pay
18Reach Company Level 10 and buy the second parcelexpansion
19Join or found a corporationthe social layer

6 · B · Every estate can play the first week

Decision: the starter kitEvery estate gets, within its four start parcels and the first parcel it can buy (Level 5): iron (as now), copper, coal, stone, a pond with a shore and a forest patch. Specialties stay, as the rich extra that makes estates different (a Copper Gulch has a big 4★ copper field, everyone else a small 2★ one).

What each estate gets

BasicSizeWhereFor
Iron ore3×3, 2★start parcelsIron Mine, Lv 2
Copper ore2×2, 2★start parcelsCopper Mine, Lv 5
Coal2×2, 2★start parcelsCoal Pit, Lv 5
Stone2×2, 2★start parcelsBrickworks, Quarry
A pond (shore)~10 tilesfirst parcelWater Pump, Sand Dredger
Forestpatchwhere it isLumber Camp

Why small and in the start parcels

A 2×2 patch holds one or two mines: enough to learn the chain and fill the first factory. A player who wants more copper buys the Copper Gulch neighbour's surplus, or the specialty parcel later. That keeps trade meaningful and estates different, while nobody is locked out of the middle game.

Parcel previews

The parcel panel lists what a parcel holds ("copper 4★, a pond, forest"), and the advisor uses it: "Parcel 6 (Level 12) has coal 4★".

7 · B · Surveyors: the starter kit without a wipe

The world's terrain is generated from a seed, so changing the generator would change land under existing buildings. The starter kit is therefore added on top, through the same mechanism Terraforming and Discoveries use: deposit seeds and terrain overrides, saved with the world.

How it works

  1. For every estate (players, tenants, free ones), the game checks which basics are missing within the start parcels and the first parcel: copper, coal, stone (a 2×2 at 2★) and a shore.
  2. For each missing one it picks a free spot: no building, pipe, gate or road on any of its tiles, not on water or a mountain, preferring grass near the HQ but at least 3 tiles from it.
  3. It adds the deposit as seeds (richness 2). A missing shore becomes a small pond (terrain override to water, about 10 tiles) in the first parcel, only on free tiles.
  4. Players get a note in their inbox: "Surveyors found copper and coal on your estate. Show me".
  5. New estates get the same when they're created, so new and old estates are equal.

Safety

RiskAnswer
Changing land under buildings or pipesNever: only free tiles, checked tile by tile.
Running twiceIdempotent: it only adds what's missing, and remembers that an estate was surveyed.
Breaking balanceSmall, poor (2★) patches; the balance simulations run before and after (§14).
Hiding something players builtA spot is only chosen on grass, beach, desert or hills with nothing on it.

8 · C · Trading: why everyone is connected

A network is every pipe and building that touch, whoever owns them. That rule is simple and great inside an estate, but across estates it joins far more than anyone meant to.

Why it happens

  • Tenants pipe all four gates, so every tenant estate bridges the corridors on all its sides.
  • A corridor pipe joins whatever it touches: one pipe from your gate to a neighbour's gate makes you part of everything that neighbour is connected to.
  • So with four players and the tenants, the district became one network: in the tester's game 68 buildings and 1,050 pipe tiles.

What it does to the game

EffectWhy it hurts
You trade with companies you never chose, 150 tiles away"Connected" means nothing: everyone is, through someone
Others' goods flow through your estate's pipesYour pipes' capacity goes to trades between others
Pump stations, a full pipe or a shortage anywhere touches everyoneYour estate's results depend on strangers
Gates make little senseOne open gate connects you to the whole district
Every change anywhere re-solves the whole districtThe solver gets slower as the district grows

9 · C · Direct partners only

Decision: no transitGoods only travel between two companies along a route that crosses nobody else's estate: the seller's estate, the corridors and wilderness, and the buyer's estate. Your trade partners are the companies you piped to yourself. Nothing of anyone else's flows through your estate.

The rules, as a player reads them

  1. You trade with a company when a pipe runs from your estate to theirs without crossing a third estate.
  2. A shared pipe in a corridor that touches the gates of three companies is a little local market: they all trade with each other.
  3. A trade happens only when it pays the seller more than their own trading post (since the play day).
  4. Your trade settings list your partners with the pipe length and how much arrives, and a switch for each (since the play day).
  5. Closing a gate cuts every route through it.

Why this and not splitting the networks

The proposal (docs/TradingRethink.md) weighed four models. The ideal one makes estates islands joined by explicit links: every network ends at its gate. It's also the most work (1–2 days) and a migration of every corridor pipe. "No transit" gives players the same rules (you trade only with who you piped to, nothing passes through your estate) with a change to how routes are found: the route between two buildings may only cross the two owners' estates. It needs no migration and keeps every pipe working. If networks ever get too big to solve quickly, the islands model is the next step; the rules players learn stay the same.

Pump stations per company

Pump stations count per company: each company needs a pump per 50 of its own buildings in a network. Your neighbours' buildings never slow your estate down.

10 · C · Gates, trade settings and the longer road

The four open questions, decided

QuestionDecisionWhy
May trade pass through a third estate (for a toll)?No in v1.1Clarity first. A toll road through estates can come back as a Toll Meter feature once the basics are clear.
A shared grid for corporation members?Later (v1.2): a corporation perkA reward for joining a corporation: members' routes may cross each other's estates.
Does a link cost more than its pipes?NoThe pipe's gold and its loss over the length are enough; distance matters already.
Must the other side accept?NoAn open gate is an invitation; each partner has a switch, and a gate can be closed.

Gates

Gates are open or closed (since the play day). The old contract and corporation gate options moved to "Who you trade with" in the trade settings. A gate is where your estate meets the corridor: a closed gate cuts every route through it.

On the map

  • Selecting a pipe shows its network as today, and the partners it reaches are outlined in their colour.
  • Hovering a gate shows "3 partners through this gate".
  • Loady's neighbour card suggests partners close enough to pay, nearest first.

11 · D · Controls: the mouse model

The right mouse button pans (and a right-click steps back). That frees the left button for what players do most: select, and drag over things to act on many at once.

InputSelect toolBuild toolPipe toolRemove tool
Left clickselect a building, pipe, gate, parcelbuild onea single pipe tileremove one
Left dragbox select buildingspaint a row or area of the buildinglay a pipe routeremove an area
Shift + click / dragadd to / remove from the selection———
Ctrl + clickselect all buildings of that type on your estate———
Double clickselect all of that type in its network———
Right clickone step back: put the tool away, clear the selection, close the panel
Right drag · middle drag · WASD · arrowspan the map
Wheel · + −zoom

Keys

V select · B build · P pipe · X remove · U upgrade the selection by one · Shift+U by ten · Del demolish the selection (asks) · Ctrl+A select all your buildings in view · Esc back · H home · N neighbours · R research · F photo mode. A ? button in the toolbar lists them.

Touch

One finger pans, two fingers zoom, tap selects. A long press starts a box selection; in the build tool a long press and drag paints. The phone layout keeps the inspector as a bottom sheet.

Why box selection first

An idle game is played in upgrades. The tester's estate has ten moilies and seven mines: upgrading them one by one is thirty clicks a visit. With a box and Upgrade all it is two, and the game can spend the gold wisely (cheapest first, so the levels stay even).

12 · D · Selecting many, painting rows

12 buildings selected
🌬Wind Moily ×10Lv 4–15
☀Solar Panel ×2Lv 3
Together+402 energy/min
Upgrade all +1 · 14.2k g +10 each · 160k g Spend 25k g, cheapest first
Select only Wind MoilyDemolish…

The selection panel

  • The buildings by type, with their level range, and what they make together.
  • Upgrade all +1 and +10 each, with the total cost; disabled with the shortfall when it's too much.
  • Spend … cheapest first: a budget (the gold you have, or a slider) goes into the cheapest upgrades one level at a time, so the selection levels evenly. The server does it in one command, so it's quick and atomic.
  • Select only one type, Demolish the selection (with the refund), and Save as blueprint when a Blueprint Office exists.
  • Selected buildings are outlined in gold on the map, with their level badges.

Painting with the build tool

Dragging with a building picks every spot along the drag (a line) or inside it (with Shift, an area) where the building fits, shows them as ghosts with the total cost, and builds them all on release: a row of solar panels in one gesture. It stops at what you can afford.

Details that matter

CaseBehaviour
A drag that starts on a buildingstill a box (no accidental moves; Move stays a button)
A tiny drag (under 6 px)a click
Others' buildings in the boxleft out (you can only act on your own); a click still inspects theirs
Pipes in the boxleft out of the selection; the Remove tool's drag removes pipes
One building in the boxthe normal building panel

13 · E · The screen: zones and rules

Every panel has a zone, and a zone holds one thing. The tester saw cards under the top bar and side panels on top of each other; both are fixed, and v1.1 makes the rule complete.

TOP · status: company, gold, level & XP, era, research, actions
LEFT · guidance: next steps, Loady, today & this week. The build menu takes its place while open.
RIGHT · one inspector: a building, the selection, a network, a gate, a parcel, a visit, the inbox
CENTRE · big windows, one at a time: research, hub, neighbours, company, corporation
BOTTOM · tools, tier bar
chat
toasts

Rules

  1. Everything starts below the top bar, which is measured (done).
  2. One inspector on the right: opening one closes the other (done). The selection panel is an inspector.
  3. One big window in the centre, over a dim backdrop; it doesn't close the inspector, so after closing it you're back where you were.
  4. Guidance yields: while the build menu is open, the left column is the build menu.
  5. Hover tips sit above the toolbar, toasts bottom right, never over the inspector.
  6. Phones: the inspector is a bottom sheet; guidance collapses to one line.

14 · Balance and pacing

The design document's targets (GDD §8.1): Level 10 on day 2–3, Level 20 in week 1, Level 30 in week 4. The typical player in the simulation after the play-day changes:

LevelTargetBefore the play dayNow
10day 2–3day 2 12hday 2 10hon target
15—day 4 13hday 4 0h
20week 1day 6 23hday 5 13hon target
25—day 13 4hday 8 12hfaster

Today's fixes (storages selling their surplus, fair trades, cheaper pipe losses) made the middle game about a third faster. That is welcome: the old middle was a grind. v1.1's starter kit adds a second and third chain from Level 5, which will make it faster still.

The plan

  • Run the three balance profiles (typical, casual, hardcore) before and after each v1.1 part.
  • Keep Level 20 in week 1 and Level 30 in week 4: if the starter kit pushes Level 30 under three weeks, raise the XP ramp (xpRamp) rather than taking rewards away.
  • The first-session simulation must still finish Loady's chapter 1 in about 20 minutes, and chapter 2 by day 2.

16 · Implementation plan

In this order: each part is small enough to ship on its own to the test server (the update overlay reloads the testers), and each is tested before the next starts.

#PartSizeChecked by
1Direct partners only (no transit), pump stations per company, partners in the trade settings½ daygame tests (A–T–C), the consistency check, balance
2Surveyors: the starter kit for existing and new estates, parcel previews, the inbox note½ daygame tests (free tiles only, idempotent), a browser look at a surveyed estate
3Controls: left-drag box select, Shift/Ctrl/double click, the selection panel with upgrade all and the budget, keys1 daybrowser scripts with real mouse drags, a server test for upgrade-all
4Next steps: the advisor on the server, the card on the left, Show me½–1 daygame tests per kind of step, the first-day simulation follows the advisor
5Level roadmap and Loady chapter 2½ daythe first-day simulation finishes chapter 2
6Painting rows with the build tool½ daybrowser script
7Screen rules: one big window over the inspector, phone check¼ daythe mobile script

For every part

  • Reproduce what it fixes in the game, then check it the same way (the rule in CLAUDE.md).
  • Game, server and frontend tests, lint, format, typecheck; CI green before the next part.
  • No wipe: new rules apply to the running world, with saved data added, never removed.
  • A short note per part to the testers, with a screenshot.

Open questions for the owner

  1. Should the advisor's steps be clickable to do them directly (upgrade now), or always open the panel first?
  2. Starter kit sizes: 2×2 at 2★ for copper, coal and stone; is that generous enough, or should coal be 3×3 (it feeds brickworks and coal plants)?
  3. Chapter 2 rewards: gold like chapter 1, or something rarer (a decoration, a manager hour)?
